front.title: Carrying PostScript in X.400 and MIME

section.name: Status of This Memo
section.t: This document specifies an Internet standards track protocol for the Internet community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements. section.name: Introduction
section.t: This document describes methods for carrying PostScript information in the two standard mail systems MIME and X.400, and the conversion between them. It uses the notational conventions of , and the conversion is further described in .
Two ways of carrying PostScript in X.400 are described. One is using the FTAM Body Part, and one uses the Extended Body Part originally described in RFC 1494.
The FTAM method is recommended.

section.name: The PostScript body part
section.t: Carrying PostScript in X.400 as an Extended Body Part was originally defined in RFC 1494. This specification carries that work forward now that RFC 1494 is obsoleted by .
The following Extended Body Part is defined for PostScript data streams. It has no parameters.
section.sourcecode: postscript-body-part EXTENDED-BODY-PART-TYPE DATA OCTET STRING ::= mime-postscript-body

section.name: The PostScript FTBP
section.t: The PostScript FTBP is identified by having the FileTransferParameters.environment.application-reference set to id-mime-ftbp-postscript.

section.name: The Application/PostScript content-type
section.t: In MIME, PostScript is carried in the body part "application/PostScript", which is defined in RFC 1521.

section.name: MIXER conversion
section.t: X.400 Body Part: Extended Body Part, OID mime-postscript-body MIME Content-Type: application/postscript Conversion Type: No conversion
The two representations of PostScript both contain a single stream of octets. This stream of octets can be copied with no problems between the representations. No other data needs to be converted.

section.name: MIXER conversion
section.t: X.400 Body Part: FTBP, OID mime-ftbp-postscript-body MIME Content-Type: application/postscript Conversion Type: No conversion
The two representations of PostScript both contain a single stream of octets. This stream of octets can be copied with no problems between the representations. No other data needs to be converted.

section.name: Security Issues
section.t: The issues concerning PostScript and security are well discussed in RFC 2046. No additional security issues are identified by this memo.
